label: input token x at original position >= 3
explanation: Fires whenever the input token is x during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase at position t >= 3; it never fires on x at positions 0-2, on <DEL>, or in the copy phase (even when x is fed back or output). Precision 1.0 and recall about 0.999 on dev; the misses are tiny (~0.01-0.02 of max) activations on non-x tokens at t=8. Magnitude rises with position: x at t=3 gives about 0.16-0.2 of max, t=4-5 about 0.4-0.6, t=6-7 about 0.6-0.8, and x at t=8 (last original slot of an L=9 sequence) reaches about 1.0. Magnitude does not depend on the preceding tokens, the first token, or digit count.

issues: No substantive issues. Test split: precision 1.0, recall 0.9989, F1 0.9994, mass recall 0.99997. The 64 test misses are all tiny activations (0.01-0.02 of max) at step 8 on non-x tokens and hold 0.0% of the mass. They look like scattered noise, not a systematic class.

The profile confirms every other claim. The feature never fires at t=0-2, on <DEL> or anywhere in the copy phase (rate 0 at t>=9 and at all recall_idx). Activation rises with position: about 0.16-0.2 at t=3, about 0.4 at t=4, and about 1.0 at t=8. Every top example is x at t=8.

Earlier tokens make no difference. Examples with x already earlier in the sequence (x z a [x], y c t x [x], m v 2 [x] ... [x]) still fire as usual. Caveat: the predicate seen(["x"]) unexpectedly matched 0 steps, even though such sequences exist. That helper seems not to work as written here, so I relied on the examples instead.
Minor: the label says 'original position >= 3' and the predicate uses t >= 3. These are the same thing in the original phase, so the label does not overclaim.
